LESSON: SPELLING INSTRUCTION

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Spelling instruction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Spelling instruction. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SPELLING INSTRUCTION
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Spelling instruction helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SPELLING INSTRUCTION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc

What this means
In this part you learn to use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Spelling instruction”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Spelling instruction is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Spelling instruction”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Spelling instruction to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Spelling instruction from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Spelling instruction: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Spelling instruction?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Spelling instruction means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use proper letter formation with (onset and rime, letter-sound correct spacing to write words correspondenc.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
